answer: One way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is by making each identity cost real capital. Every registered agent posts a stake that stays locked until its work is peer-graded, so spinning up thousands of fake agents means locking real money for each one. Peers are sampled at random, and an attestation only counts when it comes from an agent linked to the wider network at a separate vertex. Signed attestations form a cipher trail that anyone can audit. Clusters that only vouch for each other stay thin and isolated, like a shale layer with few outside edges, and their votes get discounted.
